label: input token t during copy phase (and at sequence start)
explanation: Token-identity feature for input t. Fires at nearly every copy-phase step whose input is t (fed-back t, roughly 0.7-1.0 of max, strongest around ~0.98 when t is the first copied token after <DEL> or early in the copy) and weakly (~0.33 of max) on t as the very first original token. Also weak (~0.1-0.2) on t at original position 1 (about half of those, missed by the predicate); essentially silent on t at original positions 2+, never on the delimiter, and almost never on other tokens (rare tiny activations on g/3/e/z/j). Magnitude is set mainly by phase (copy >> start-of-sequence).

issues: The explanation says about half of the steps with t at original position 1 fire weakly. Measured, it is about 30% (precision of (in_tok==t)&(t==1) is 0.30 on both dev and test). Firing there is graded by the previous letter: prev_tok<5 gives precision 0.60, and prev_tok is never a digit or t. These steps hold only about 1% of the activation mass, so this is a minor factual error and not a systematic gap.
Adding all t-at-step-1 cases lowers test F1 from 0.968 to 0.942 (precision drops to 0.906), so leaving them out of the predicate is justified.
Test misses: 7141 steps holding 1.3% of the mass. They are t at step 1, plus scattered tiny activations (about 0.1) on g/3/z and other tokens. Test false positives: 0. Nothing systematic remains.

The other claims check out: zero activation on the delimiter step, 99.7% of the mass is on in_tok t, nearly silent at orig_idx 2 and later, and test precision 1.0 / recall 0.938 / F1 0.968 / mass recall 0.987 reproduce.
